correctness.rationale: For θ=∛2 put β=2q+p₂θ+p₁θ², a nonzero algebraic integer since q≥1 and (1,θ,θ²) is a basis. Writing S=θ+θ² and Δ=max(|qθ−p₁|,|qθ²−p₂|), its real embedding is bounded by 6q+SΔ and its two complex embeddings by SΔ: the leading q terms cancel by 1+ω+ω²=0. Its integer norm has modulus ≥1. For Δ≤1 this gives Δ≥[S²(6+S)q]⁻¹/²>(1/9)q⁻¹/² since S<57/20 and (57/20)²(177/20)<81. For Δ>1 this lower bound is immediate. This proves the original all-q claim without the announced finite verification. In the primal Dani normalization the nonzero-q norms are ≥max(s,c/√s) for s=|q|e⁻ᵗ, so are ≥c²/³; q=0 gives ≥1 for t≥0. For the dual, let N denote the sup norm of a lattice vector and K=1+S. The linear form L in the frozen proof satisfies N≥eᵗ|L|, H(a)≤K e^(t/2)N, and |L|≥1/(K²H²) by the norm argument. Thus N³≥K⁻⁴ and K<3.85 yields N>1/10. The displayed dual bound is a separately proved conclusion, not an equivalent restatement of the 1/500 inequality. The universal algebraic-vector characterization in the context is not valid; the cubic-basis theorem here does not require it.
residual_risks: The frozen finite-range and float-scan scripts were not supplied; the independent exact norm argument replaces their role for the main inequalities. No optimal constant has been verified.
